newsitem.title: USA: Salt Lake Cty MBA, Utah, revs AA-minus - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Salt Lake Cty MBA, Utah, revs AA-minus - Fitch.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 18 - Salt Lake County Municipal Building Authority's (UT.) $13.9 million lease revenue bonds, series 1996A, are rated 'AA-' by Fitch Investors Service. The bonds, dated Oct. 15, 1996 are scheduled to be sold competitively Oct. 29, 1996.

Additionally, the $64.7 million lease revenue bonds and the $121.2 million general obligation bonds are affirmed 'AA-' and 'AAA', respectively. The rating reflects the county's ability to annually appropriate amounts required under the lease securing the bonds, low debt levels, strong financial operations and economy.

The bonds are additionally secured by a leasehold interest on all three authority projects. Rental payments are expected to be funded from the operating revenues of the county's eight golf courses. The golf course system has had a record of positive financial operations and the unreserved golf course enterprise fund balance was $5.3 million in 1995. Lease provisions are good, but the rental payments are subject to annual lease renewals and appropriations by the county. The county has had a long history of conservative fiscal policies and budgeting practices, which have resulted in strong financial performance and flexibility.

Between 1990 and 1994, the county has had net operating surpluses and undesignated general fund balances that have exceeded 16% of general fund expenditures. Fiscal 1995 ended with a $1.7 million net operating deficit, which was a planned drawdown. Overall debt burden is low. The county's economic outlook continues to be favorable. The 1995 unemployment rate was a low 3.1%, as compared to the state and national rates at 3.6% and 5.6%, respectively.
